prompt:
ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mythics illustration of SERKET, the Egyptian protective goddess who binds and contains the snake deity Apep, guarding the turn of the underworld path.
ANATOMY: one fully clothed WOMAN, one human head, exactly TWO arms and TWO legs under an opaque floor-length linen robe, covered chest and shoulders; ONE distinct realistic SCORPION atop her head as clearly readable emblem, large spread pincers and a hooked tail above the crown of her head. One hand holds a large ANKH, the other hand grips a WAS-SCEPTRE. No scorpion hybrid body. [serket-c02]
MOMENT: bracing forward toward the viewer as she contains ONE dark serpent across the stone path at her feet, the was-sceptre presses down on the serpent's coiled body, her ankh lifted boldly, fierce protective downward gaze. The serpent struggles within tight coils beneath her authority. [serket-c05]
POWER: documented binding/containment of Apep represented physically by held-down serpent, not glowing bonds, rays or invented magic. She guards the pathway bend and funerary canopic vessels. [serket-c04,serket-c05]
SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low angle near the path; goddess fills four fifths of frame, head and oversized perspective emblem clearly readable against dark vault; held ankh and sceptre unmistakable foreground silhouettes; no tiny humans, no claim of literal giant size.
LIGHT & WEATHER: one low architectural amber brazier casts sharp rim light across face, scorpion and hands; black shadows, natural dust, underworld darkness.
SURFACE: creased opaque linen, tarnished gold ankh, worn dark staff, rough stone and matte snake scales.
SETTING: bend in underworld stone pathway with a few distant canopic vessels. [serket-c04,serket-c05]
MOOD: formidable divine protector, controlling dangerous serpent, awe-inspiring and unyielding, never a calm ordinary woman or monster goddess.
HARD CONSTRAINTS: one human head, two arms, single scorpion on head, one serpent below; no text, lettering, glyphs, logo, border, frame or watermark; no extra heads, limbs or fingers; no film/game/anime/comic design; no nudity or gore; no generic glow aura, neon outline, energy ribbons or venom lasers.
TARGETED CONSTRAINT: all clothing is COMPLETELY UNDECORATED plain ivory linen, simple uninscribed gold cuffs, absolutely NO sash, symbols, glyph-like motifs, embroidery or writing. Architecture is plain uninscribed stone with no carved wall reliefs. Keep the two-arm protective action, scorpion, ankh, was-sceptre and contained serpent.
depicted_variant: Woman with scorpion, ankh and was-sceptre physically containing Apep at the underworld path bend.

visual_requirements.description: Woman with scorpion on head, ankh in one hand and was-sceptre in the other, opaque clothing.
Physical containment of the snake deity Apep, explicitly documented in exact quote c05; no invented emitted spell.
Underworld pathway bend and canopic vessels reflect guardian and funerary roles.

aura: Formidable containment of serpent Apep and path guarding (serket-c05), clear scorpion/ankh/was-sceptre (serket-c02) and funerary role (serket-c04); natural brazier lighting rather than emitted spells.
artistic_choices: Sceptre physically pinning Apep represents documented binding/containment; method of contact and serpent appearance are restrained editorial staging, not an asserted spell.
Plain opaque ivory linen and uninscribed cuffs correct first generation's pseudo-writing.
Low camera gives towering authority without a claimed gigantic body; head scorpion rendered as oversized readable attribute as required for divine iconography.
Brazier is architectural ambient light, not goddess-emitted fire.

visual_review.notes: Native inspected: one covered two-arm woman, one scorpion atop head with two pincers and curled tail, clear ankh and was-sceptre in separate hands; staff contains one coiled snake, one snake head. Active containment and extreme low camera give awe at thumbnail. Plain cloth/stone has no pseudo-writing, no text/aura/gore. First attempt retained for lettering failure.

rationale: Big names (major gods, archangels, demon princes, primordial monsters, famous literary beings) must look imposing and powerful: an epic, awe-inspiring or terrifying presence that matches their standing in the tradition.

rejected_attempts.reason: Ordinary woman with a scorpion emblem at human scale.
Codex native rejection: gold pseudo-hieroglyphic markings on sash violate no-lettering constraint; regenerate with undecorated cloth and masonry.

root_visual_review.notes: Serket with scorpion crown, ankh and was-sceptre pins the coiled Apep beneath her in the underworld; monumental and threatening.
